research_board.rationale: Retained central role: 11 targets, nine catches and 153 yards. Assess a fresh price against Williams and LaPorta rather than extrapolating the yardage.
Candidate beyond the prior nine: nine targets, five catches and 91 yards show involvement beyond his two touchdowns. Compare his eventual price with St. Brown and the weaker LaPorta allocation.
17 carries and seven targets/six catches supplied both rushing and receiving opportunity. Recheck Hall's status and the split before assigning repeat volume.
25 carries and three targets justify renewed study. His three touchdowns and rushing bonus drove the score; they are not a repeatable point floor.
Another candidate beyond the prior nine: 24 carries, but Tampa Bay ran 49 times and Gainwell had 14 carries. Evaluate the split under a less favorable script and Mayfield's health.
Five of 11 team targets supported a role, not enough absolute volume. Requires a new price, Mayfield health and Week 8 availability checks.
Three targets in 22 team attempts challenged the prior double-digit-target extrapolation. Keep as a question rather than automatically restoring him.

summary: Week 8 opens with an unpriced research board. Detroit target allocation and the Pollard/Braelon workloads warrant fresh investigation; no Week 7 salary is reused. Five of the frozen nine are unavailable to this Sunday window through byes or Thursday scheduling.
counterargument: One game's usage is unstable. Detroit target competition, Hall's availability and Tampa Bay's extreme run-heavy script could change the apparent values once prices and current availability are known.
